questions.question: 35312. Which marketing orientation is MOST likely to invest in advanced data analytics for customer behavior tracking?
questions.explain:
Customer concept firms seek to understand and personalize offerings using detailed data to maximize CLV.

questions.question: 35311. A Bangladeshi dairy brand adopts eco-friendly packaging because consumers are increasingly concerned about sustainability. This reflects:
questions.explain:
This aligns with the societal marketing principle of balancing consumer satisfaction and environmental concerns.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 38.

questions.question: 35310. “We must persuade customers to buy our product through aggressive promotion; otherwise, they won’t.” This is:
questions.explain:
The selling concept is built on heavy promotion and sales tactics, especially for unsought goods.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 37.

questions.question: 35309. Which orientation would prioritize building long-term trust even at the cost of short-term sales?
questions.explain:
The customer concept emphasizes lifetime value, loyalty, and trust, over short-term volume.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 40.

questions.question: 35308. Which crop contains gluten?

questions.question: 35307. Which is the correct link between needs, wants, and demands?
questions.option1: Needs are shaped by culture; wants are basic human requirements
questions.option2: Needs are basic; wants are culture-shaped; demands are wants with buying power
questions.option3: Needs are created by marketing; wants are innate
questions.explain:
This is the standard hierarchy: basic needs → shaped into wants → become demands when backed by ability to pay.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 32.

questions.question: 35306. Which core concept reflects the benefit a customer gets minus the cost to obtain it?
questions.explain:
Perceived value = total benefits – total costs. Satisfaction measures how well performance matches expectations, and exchange is the act of trade.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 33.

questions.question: 35305. A company states: “We aim to increase customer satisfaction, but if customers want harmful products, we will not provide them.” This reflects:
questions.explain:
Societal marketing applies an ethical filter to the marketing concept to protect long-term societal welfare.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 38.

questions.question: 35304. Which approach is MOST vulnerable to competition in an era of rapid technological change?
questions.explain:
Product-oriented firms may invest heavily in features that are quickly outdated, missing shifts in customer needs.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 36.

questions.question: 35303. A high-end electronics store focuses only on customers with above-average income and invests in premium experiences. This is an example of:
questions.explain:
This reflects the customer concept applied to a specific high-value segment, aiming to maximize profitability from them.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 40.

questions.question: 35302. Which is NOT an element of Kotler’s core marketing concepts?
questions.explain:
Factory efficiency is part of production management, not a core marketing concept.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, pp. 32–33.

questions.question: 35301.  “Delivering value to customers in ways that maintain or improve both the customer’s and society’s well-being” refers to:
questions.explain:
This is the textbook definition of societal marketing — balancing company profits, consumer wants, and societal interests.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 38.

questions.question: 35300. Dapog nursery bed is generally suitable for which areas?

questions.question: 35299. Which orientation is MOST suitable for a monopolistic utility provider in Bangladesh (e.g., electricity)?
questions.explain:
With little competition and guaranteed demand, focus is typically on efficiency, cost control, and availability — hallmarks of the production concept.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 35.

questions.question: 35298. Which orientation fits best: “We focus on retaining profitable customers and growing share of wallet through CRM”?
questions.explain:
The customer/market concept extends the marketing concept by emphasizing not just satisfaction but maximizing the value of each customer relationship over time.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 40.

questions.question: 35297. Which core marketing concept emphasizes “what customers will give up to get the product”?
questions.explain:
Explanation: Exchange is the act of obtaining a desired object from someone by offering something in return (often money, time, or effort). Needs and value are related but are not the transactional act itself.

questions.question: 35296. A company launching a healthier but more expensive biscuit without researching price sensitivity is likely falling into:
questions.explain:
This is a classic example of over-focusing on product quality (health benefits) while ignoring customer affordability and demand research.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, pp. 36–37.

questions.question: 35295. Which is a limitation of the product concept?
questions.option2: Overemphasis on quality and features while ignoring customer needs
questions.explain:
The product concept assumes customers will choose products with the best quality/features, which risks “marketing myopia” if the features don’t match what customers value most.
References: Kotler et al. (2022)

questions.question: 35294. In the marketing concept, the correct sequence is:
questions.option2: Market → Customer needs → Integrated marketing → Profits via satisfaction
questions.option4: Capacity → Efficiency → Low prices → Profit via scale
questions.explain:
The marketing concept is an outside-in approach: it starts with the market, identifies customer needs, integrates the marketing mix to satisfy them, and achieves profits through satisfaction. Options A and D are inside-out (production/selling concepts), and C reflects product concept thinking.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 37

questions.question: 35293. Which is a key risk of the production concept in modern markets?
questions.explain:
Overemphasizing efficiency and cost can compromise quality and responsiveness to customer needs.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 35.

questions.question: 35292. Which is an example of customer lifetime value (CLV) thinking?
questions.option1: Offering discounts to close today’s sale only
questions.option2: Investing in loyalty programs to retain high-value clients

CLV emphasizes long-term profitability from customer relationships, not just short-term transactions.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 41.

questions.question: 35291.  Which concept assumes customers must be persuaded to buy through aggressive selling?
questions.explain:
The selling concept focuses on sales volume through promotion, especially for unsought goods.
References: Kotler et al. (2022), Ch. 1, p. 37.

questions.question: 35290. A bank introduces green loans for eco-friendly projects, ensuring both profitability and environmental sustainability. This is an example of:

questions.question: 35289.  Which is NOT part of the marketing process?

While efficiency supports marketing, maximizing factory utilization is an operational goal, not part of Kotler’s 5-step marketing process.

questions.question: 35288. Which orientation adds society’s long-term interests to the marketing concept?
questions.explain:
The societal marketing concept balances company profits, consumer satisfaction, and societal well-being. It goes beyond the marketing concept by adding a third dimension.

questions.question: 35282. The sugarcane and potato is an intercropping system of-
questions.explain:
The sugarcane and potato intercropping system is primarily associated with the autumn season.This is because sugarcane is a long-duration crop, and when planted in the autumn (typically in October), its initial growth is slow due to the onset of winter. This leaves a significant amount of space between the rows of sugarcane that can be effectively utilized for growing a short-duration crop like potato.

questions.question: 35278. What action should be taken when the leaf color is lighter than the threshold on the LCC?
questions.explain:
A Leaf Color Chart (LCC) is a simple tool used to assess the nitrogen status of a crop, particularly rice , by matching the color of a plant's leaf to a color chart. It is a visual and qualitative way to determine if a crop needs additional nitrogen fertilizer.
The LCC typically consists of a plastic ruler-like strip with four to six color shades ranging from yellowish-green to dark green. The colors correspond to different levels of nitrogen in the plant.
